.qc-cache/coldwater-2026-10-01-history-hardening-r3/task/task.toml, environment/Dockerfile, tests/test.sh and five judge.toml files
evidence: Arithmetic passes on the exact frozen bytes: task.toml:18,21,27 sets agent 7200 s, cold environment build 600 s and verifier 13200 s. tests/test.sh:207,213,224 runs RewardKit with max-concurrent-agent 1, gates 1500 s then scored 11100 s. Gate judge.toml:4 values are 600+600=1200<1500; scored judge.toml:4 values are 9000+900+900=10800<11100; 1500+11100=12600<13200, leaving 600 s for launch, liveness, substitution and scoring. Liveness at tests/test.sh:42-53,116-123 retries 120 times using at most two 2-second URL reads per probe and 0.25-second sleeps; its real duration was not measured in a configured run. Frozen template settings match. Evidence/11/audit.json verifies all 43 frozen task, 34 frozen rule and 77 raw-index artifact hashes with zero mismatches, and finds no indexed rewardkit.log or run-root runtime-evidence.json. The indexed local-proof-summary.json:7-17 gives scripted browser phases of 122.587, 5.408 and 1.410 seconds, but explicitly says at lines 43-46 that configured judge elapsed duration was not measured. preflight.json's 'timeout nesting' result explicitly says arithmetic only. No exact-current cold image build, agent build, full functional judge or full verifier duration establishes that these allowances fit the 82 functional criteria. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:25,31 and qc/README.md:27 require measured, hash-bound runtime evidence before clearance. A fast dead app can terminate at the gates and falsely make the budgets look sufficient; a conforming app exercising all 82 functional checks, restart and browser interactions could hit a judge or suite timeout and lose valid credit. This remains an evidence gap, not a demonstrated timeout defect.
counterexample: A broken app that answers the health URL but fails the render gate ends before the 82-criterion functional judge, so a short run cannot validate workload fit. Conversely, a conforming implementation could pass the gates and still lose credit if the full functional judge needs more than 9000 seconds or suite setup consumes the 300-second scored headroom; no configured timing run resolves either case.
suggested_fix: Measure an exact-current cold build and complete configured verifier run against a conforming app, preserving hash-bound raw logs with per-judge, suite, liveness and total elapsed times; retain canonical limits unless the measurements justify a specific authorized change below five hours.
